long_biography.plain_text:
During a summer on Antiparos, Komninou and her infant daughter rented a house and found a lasting sense of belonging. The choice redirected a life that had moved from fine-art and design studies in London to work at interiors magazines in Athens. At Livadia Bay, she bought a summer home, gradually assembled nearby plots and rejected more conventional resort plans.

The project took eight years to evolve from nine rental houses into a hotel of villas, dining spaces, a farm and a wellness retreat. Komninou worked with architect Fania Sinanioti, insisting on local stone, indigenous planting, privacy and restraint rather than a standard Cycladic look. At Apantima Beach, The Beach House now operates as the smaller sister property.
